blogs.title: How LLMs Can Be Turned Into Feature Engineers for Tabular Data
blogs.description: An overview of the FeatLLM framework, explaining how large language models are repurposed to generate rule‑based features instead of making direct predictions, and why this reduces inference cost and sidesteps prompt‑size limits.

blogs.title: From Rules to Numbers: Turning Natural‑Language Conditions into Machine‑Learning Features
blogs.description: A deep dive into the two‑step prompting strategy used by FeatLLM, covering how the model extracts logical rules, parses them into executable code, and creates binary features that feed a simple linear model.

blogs.title: Bagging, Ensembles, and the Fight Against Spurious Correlations in Low‑Shot Tabular Learning
blogs.description: Explains the ensemble and feature‑bagging techniques introduced in FeatLLM, illustrating how they improve robustness, handle high‑dimensional tables, and protect against noisy or irrelevant columns.

blogs.title: Benchmarking FeatLLM: Few‑Shot Performance Across 13 Real‑World Datasets
blogs.description: Summarizes the experimental results, comparing FeatLLM with traditional models (LogReg, XGBoost, Random Forest) and other LLM‑based approaches (TabLLM, STUNT, TABLET), highlighting its 10% average AUC gain in low‑shot regimes.

blogs.title: Practical Guide: Deploying FeatLLM with Only API Access to GPT‑3.5
blogs.description: Step‑by‑step instructions for data scientists to set up the FeatLLM pipeline—prompt design, rule extraction, code generation, linear weight tuning, and ensemble voting—without needing model fine‑tuning or large GPU resources.
